---
title: "Scrape: recessions"
engine: knitr
---

The "List of recessions in the United States" table has a flat header, so renaming the columns is the only reshaping it needs. In R, `httr2` fetches the page, `rvest::html_table()` parses every table on it, and `Filter()` keeps the one with "GDP decline" in its header. In Python, `requests` fetches the page, then `pandas.read_html()` finds every table and `match=` picks out the same one.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: scrape-recessions-r
#| eval: false
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(readr)

html <- request("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_recessions_in_the_United_States") |>
  req_user_agent("wikimill-project/0.1") |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_html()

tables <- html_table(html)
recessions <- Filter(\(t) any(grepl("GDP decline", names(t))), tables)[[1]]
names(recessions) <- c(
  "name", "period_range", "duration", "time_since_previous",
  "peak_unemployment", "gdp_decline", "characteristics"
)
write_csv(recessions, "data/recessions.csv")
head(recessions)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: scrape-recessions-py
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_recessions_in_the_United_States"
html = requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}).text

tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(html), match="GDP decline")
recessions = tables[0]
recessions.columns = [
    "name", "period_range", "duration", "time_since_previous",
    "peak_unemployment", "gdp_decline", "characteristics"
]
recessions.to_csv("data/recessions.csv", index=False)
recessions.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Either works

Both versions take about the same code. One difference shows up in the raw text: `html_table()` joins text across a `<br>` tag without a space (`3 years1 month`), while `read_html()` inserts one. The cleaning step only parses `period_range` and the percentages, so both CSVs produce the same cleaned table.
:::

These chunks are shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `Rscript src/scrape_recessions.R` or `python src/scrape_recessions.py` from the project root to refresh `data/recessions.csv`. See [clean_recessions.qmd](clean_recessions.qmd) for the next step.
